Thirty-three comments

Richard Dwyer’s

Thank you Binioubraz for posting this tune. It is an awe inspiring tune (not that I play it anything but only vaguely like either of these versions). It is amazing that it has been recorded by so many ITM musicians. It is simply a knock out of a tune. Fabulous.
PS: I play it with a G# (bar 4) an F natural (bar 5) in part A. I usually like to roll a couple of times each tune, but not in this one. I don’t think it should be played too fast. I think it is a real listening to it tune. Lovely.

Anyway, Kenny, I’ll post his recording in the recording section -- I didn’t realize it wasn’t there already. The recording has all those great tunes he’s written. Personally it’s not my cup of tea, but Dow might enjoy it. No one can dispute that Richard Dwyer is one of the great living composers of today though.

Re: Richard Dwyer’s

Hi Gillies - to begin with, the “Richard Dwyer’s” reel recorded by “Wolfstone” has nothing whatsoever musically to do with the tune sheet music above. The only thing they share is the name “Richard Dwyer’s”.
This is a mystery tune which no-one has been able to identify the source of yet. It was made famous more, I would suggest, by Jarlath Henderson and Ross Ainslie when they recorded it. It has been recorded in a medley by the “Field Marshall Montgomery” Pipe Band from the North of Ireland, but there doesn’t seem to be any information as to the origins of the tune on anybody’s sleeve notes. This being a website dedicated to Irish traditional music, everyone assumed that it was a composition of Richard Dwyer from Co. Cork. No one has provided any evidence for this, and I wonder if there is another Richard Dwyer out there, possibly a Highland piper, who may have composed it. Again, this is a pure guess on my part, with no evidence. The answer possibly lies with the “FMM Pipe Band”, if someone knew how to contact them.
See comments here :
https://thesession.org/tunes/8453

Richard Dwyer’s, X:9

I have been lucky to listen to Richie Dwyer playing that tune recently in a bar for the last Michael Dywer Festival in Allihies june 9th, 2024. Even he is now 88, he still play very fine with a box in Eflat to be on his own. ;)
As said by Phantom Button 18 years ago, Richie record this reel on his CD “In the creative mood” which is now available on youtube. Because he impress me a lot in Allihies, I’ve taken enough time to write down this setting which is pretty close of his first playing on his CD (sorry , only the first time… :) ) As I’ve said, he was playing his Eflat box, so the tune on the CD is originaly in Bflat Dorian… It’s up to you.
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=eQvA2Tfr_Io&list=OLAK5uy_lgFungY9xSALf5c0JyX7qZTOXMI9tKPgA&index=2
